A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carbonation of a beverage slows gastric emptying, and that this effect is independent of the beverage's carbohydrate content.
carbonation content is a significant predictor of gastric volume and emptying, whereas carbohydrate content is not.

the rate of gastric emptying is primarily determined by the carbonation content of a beverage, and that the ingestion of carbonated beverages prior to body composition measurements can produce a significant error.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carbonation content is the major determinant of gastric emptying and gastric distress.
the presence of carbonation in beverages can significantly alter gastric emptying and thus the timing and severity of gastric distress.
carbonated beverages, such as CC, can be used to induce a large gastric gas load, which can be measured using MRI.
